papers.title: Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models
key_contributions: Unified token-based representation for images and text using VQGAN tokenizer
Single transformer handles both understanding and generation
QK-Norm and dropout for training stability in mixed-modal setting
State-of-the-art on VQA and image captioning benchmarks
Human evaluation shows mixed-modal generation capability
limitations: Single tokenizer must serve both understanding and generation - compromises both
Poor OCR capability due to tokenizer weakness with text
Training instability from modality competition in softmax
No dedicated understanding pathway - uses same discrete tokens for everything

papers.title: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning
key_contributions: Connects CLIP vision encoder to LLM via projection layer
Two-stage training: feature alignment then end-to-end fine-tuning
Strong multimodal chat and reasoning capabilities
limitations: Understanding only - no image generation capability
No shared representation with generation tasks

papers.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
key_contributions: Pairwise sigmoid loss as simpler alternative to softmax contrastive loss
Decouples batch size from loss computation
papers.relevance: Sigmoid loss can be used in DVE to handle mixed continuous/discrete token contrastive alignment

papers.title: LlamaGen: Autoregressive Model Beats Diffusion for Image Generation
key_contributions: Vanilla autoregressive models can match diffusion for image generation
Well-designed VQGAN tokenizer (codebook dim=8, size=16384) achieves 0.94 rFID
Classifier-free guidance adapted for autoregressive models
Llama architecture with 2D RoPE for image generation
papers.relevance: Provides generation pathway design for DVE; validates autoregressive approach

gap_analysis: No existing work provides both strong multimodal understanding AND visual generation with a dedicated encoding strategy for each. Chameleon uses one tokenizer for both (compromising quality), LLaVA only does understanding, and LlamaGen only does generation. DVE fills this gap by decoupling visual encoding into understanding (continuous) and generation (discrete) pathways that share a common backbone.
